designPrinciple: A beginner first receives bounded explanation or demonstration, then predicts and inspects a browser result, practices in a safe fixed context, passes a source-mapped Skill Check, builds a progressively less scaffolded artifact, repairs one reproducible defect, verifies exact cases, and records human-reviewable Proof.
targetLearner: A tertiary fresher or independent beginner with basic computer literacy and no assumed coding experience
technologySequence: Windows VS Code, current browser, DevTools, localhost preview, Git, and GitHub setup
HTML document metadata, landmarks, headings, links, local media, validation, and keyboard navigation
CSS cascade, inheritance, custom properties, box model, readable typography, contrast, and computed evidence
Flexbox, Grid, fluid media, mobile-first breakpoints, overflow, reflow, and zoom
browser JavaScript bindings, conditions, named functions, DOM selection/update, native controls, and events
arrays, record objects, canonical state, derived views, event delegation, JSON, and localStorage
semantic forms, native constraints, accessible errors/status, keyboard, focus, and manual checks
fetch, response.ok, JSON validation, request states, retry, Console, and Network diagnosis
integrated verification, Git, README, GitHub Pages, and live-path checks
learningRhythm: active interaction, prediction, inspection, validation, or comparison
required Build in sessions of at most two hours

resourceRoleStrategy.learn: A short first explanation or visual demonstration.
resourceRoleStrategy.practice: An observable interaction, edit, prediction, inspection, validator, DevTools, or accessibility exercise.
resourceRoleStrategy.reference: A precise bounded web-platform or tool lookup beside immediate work, never an unscoped documentation dump.

progressionPolicy: Weeks 1-3 establish structure, styling, and responsive layout without a calculator or programming-first jump.
Weeks 4-7 add one browser behavior layer at a time: events, canonical state/storage, forms/accessibility, then HTTP data and failure states.
Week 8 introduces only bounded recovery and static publication while integrating already practiced application behavior.
workloadPrinciples: Eight instructional Weeks at six hours each.
Setup is separate and skippable only through explicit verification.
No Build session exceeds two hours.
Most time is reserved for editing, previewing, inspecting, validating, debugging, testing, evidence, and explanation rather than passive consumption.
assessmentPolicy: Each Week has ten independently authored, source-mapped questions; 7/10 passes; attempts are unlimited; option order reshuffles per attempt; browser competence is judged through Build and Proof, not quiz score alone.

projectArchitecture.title: Web Foundations Practice Portfolio
projectArchitecture.outcome: Produce seven progressively stronger browser artifacts demonstrating semantic HTML, CSS systems, responsive layout, DOM events, canonical state, local persistence, accessible forms, fetch states, and evidence-led debugging.

projectArchitecture.title: FreshStart Hub
projectArchitecture.outcome: Deliver a documented, responsive, accessible static orientation application with local JSON, filtering, saved events, honest request states, a verified test record, Git history, and a working GitHub Pages URL.
